detailed_summary: The paper addresses a fundamental open problem in quantum nonlocality: whether maximally entangled states are sufficient for perfect strategies in bipartite pseudo-telepathic games. The authors construct a counterexample, a bipartite nonlocal game with input sets of sizes 4 and 3 and output sets both of size 6, that admits a perfect entangled strategy but no perfect strategy using a maximally entangled state. This game belongs to a new class of games called 'inner product games,' which may have independent interest. The result resolves a long-standing question in the negative, showing that maximally entangled states are not complete for such games.
key_contributions: Provides the first counterexample to the conjecture that maximally entangled states are complete for bipartite pseudo-telepathic games.
Introduces a new class of nonlocal games, termed 'inner product games,' which may be useful for studying quantum nonlocality and entanglement.
Constructs an explicit game with small input/output sizes (4x3 inputs, 6x6 outputs) that demonstrates the gap between general entangled strategies and those using maximally entangled states.
Offers a concrete example that can guide future research on the role of entanglement in quantum advantage.
